1.explanation: The root of the problem is in the Python language definition (src/languages/python.js), which declares “def” as a keyword and relies on a generated regex to detect standalone keywords. That regex is produced by compile_keywords.js (src/lib/compile_keywords.js) using word-boundary markers. In the new version the boundary logic is too permissive, causing “def” at the end of “_undef” to be recognized as a separate keyword. Fixing or tightening the keyword-matching regex in compile_keywords.js (or overriding it in python.js) will stop “def” from matching inside longer identifiers.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting Python code (highlight.js v11.3.1), an identifier that ends in “def” (for example “_undef”) is split so that the trailing “def” is colored as if it were the Python “def” keyword. Everything after that point is parsed as keyword content and the rest of the identifier is not rendered correctly. This does not occur in v10.7.3 and other highlighters do not exhibit it. The attached screenshot shows “foo = _undef” instead of treating “_undef” as a single identifier.

2.explanation:
1. compile_keywords.js: This utility builds the final regexes for all language keywords using custom look-around definitions. It currently treats underscores as breaking word boundaries, which makes the tail “def” in “_undef” match the Python keyword pattern. We need to adjust its boundary logic to include underscore as a word character.
2. python.js: The Python language definition lists ‘def’ among its keywords via compileKeywords. Fixing compile_keywords.js will correct python.js, but if any Python-specific keyword rules override defaults, they may also need adjustment here.
3. python-repl.js: The REPL mode for Python reuses the same keyword-compilation logic. To keep consistent behavior in interactive snippets, its configuration should also use the improved boundary definitions so that _undef never splits.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting Python code in highlight.js v11+, an identifier named “_undef” is mis-tokenized so that the trailing “def” is colored as the Python keyword def. In the screenshot you can see foo = _undef – the atom _undef should be entirely a plain identifier, not half plain and half keyword. This happens because highlight.js generates keyword-matching regexes that treat underscore _ as a non-word character boundary, so “def” inside “_undef” looks like a standalone keyword.
